Sofia.review: Works: one continuous outline, both lines leave the start heading right, big S-neck reads as a swan, no detached eye. Change: keep the neck curves gentle with no sharp kinks, and make the two lines meet cleanly at the beak tip. Keep strokes long, as few joins as possible. Optional: a small tail point at the left would help.

Omar.thinking: Draft looks buildable: two lines from the tail, start angles about 75 degrees apart, which is fine. The only weak spot is the sharp kink where the back line turns up into the neck. Review it, then dry run once it's locked.
Omar.review: Nice, I like it. Two lines from the tail leave START about 75 degrees apart, so that's fine, and no floating bits. One fix: where the upper line comes off the back and turns up into the neck, the corner is too tight. Round it into a smooth sweep, a bit more room before it heads up, or the fall stops there. Same on the head: keep the turn into the beak soft. The two lines meeting at the beak tip is fine. If you can, make the neck a touch longer and more S-shaped so it reads swan, not duck. Otherwise good to lock. Sofia and I can take one line each, and I'll take the start.

reviews.Sofia: Works: one continuous outline, both lines leave the start heading right, big S-neck reads as a swan, no detached eye. Change: keep the neck curves gentle with no sharp kinks, and make the two lines meet cleanly at the beak tip. Keep strokes long, as few joins as possible. Optional: a small tail point at the left would help.
reviews.Omar: Nice, I like it. Two lines from the tail leave START about 75 degrees apart, so that's fine, and no floating bits. One fix: where the upper line comes off the back and turns up into the neck, the corner is too tight. Round it into a smooth sweep, a bit more room before it heads up, or the fall stops there. Same on the head: keep the turn into the beak soft. The two lines meeting at the beak tip is fine. If you can, make the neck a touch longer and more S-shaped so it reads swan, not duck. Otherwise good to lock. Sofia and I can take one line each, and I'll take the start.
reviews.Jack: Body and two-line split from the tail work well. Change: make the neck slimmer, taller and more S-curved (it reads duck-like now), keep head small with a clear beak pointing right, lift the tail tip slightly. Client wants graceful and long-necked, no fish. Otherwise approve.

recap:
A swan for a rowing club by a lake: that was the brief. Jack met the client, who wanted a graceful bird with a long, elegant neck, and Hana drafted it in side view. Jack's review asked for a slimmer, taller S-curve, and Hana took every note. When the client loved the swan but found the neck thick and stubby, Hana redrew the neck and took it on herself.

Sofia laid the back line while Omar built the front line from the start. The turning point came when the team learned that nothing would fall without the start domino at the tail. Hana reminded Omar, "start domino first please," and he put it in. Sofia and Jack then hunted for breaks near the tail, nudging dominoes back into line.

Time ran short. Jack asked for "tiny fixes only," and Omar kept laying the front line. When the clock ran out, 9 of 111 dominoes fell. Everyone still called it a swan.
